data_source.description: Synthetic demo store data persisted in PostgreSQL. All metrics are computed from database records; no live merchant is connected.

assumptions: Hypothetical aggregate scenario, not a prediction or guaranteed business outcome.
The selected historical period's product mix, net merchandise basket, and refund/restock pattern remain constant per expected order.
Revenue is VAT-exclusive and already reflects historical discounts and dated refunds; VAT is not removed again.
Selling-price change applies first, then the additional scenario discount; historical discounts are not applied twice. Customer shipping charges do not receive these price changes.

Expected order volume and visitors are fractional expectations rounded to six decimal places; the same published order volume scales revenue and variable costs. Money rounds HALF_UP to currency cents per component.
Net historical COGS scales with expected order volume and unit-cost change. Carrier shipping, platform fees and customer shipping revenue scale with order volume at the observed per-order mix.
Employee, rent and other operating expenses remain fixed for the selected period; additional operating expense is added to other expenses.
Advertising uses historical AdSpend plus the explicit currency change and does not scale with orders; mirrored advertising expenses are excluded by the finance engine.
Conversion is a separate user assumption, or the exact historical orders-to-visitors ratio when left unchanged; price, discount and advertising changes do not automatically change it.
Operating profit follows the financial report definition and is not accounting net profit. Unrecorded costs and existing accounting limitations remain outside the model.

assumptions: Recommendations are the highest operating-profit candidates in the tested grid, under the stated assumptions and constraints; they are not guaranteed real-world optimal strategies.
Conversion, visitor change and unit-cost change are fixed user assumptions across all candidates. Conversion is not an independently optimized business decision.
The model has no validated price-demand relationship: prices, discounts and advertising do not automatically change conversion or visitors. Actual customer responses remain unknown.
Advertising increases and additional operating expenses are optional spending decisions. Without an assumed behavioral benefit, added spending reduces operating profit in this model.

With conversion and traffic held fixed, the grid often favors the highest permitted price and the lowest discount or optional spend. This is a model consequence, not validated evidence that demand will remain unchanged.
The grid includes range endpoints and evenly spaced rounded values. It can miss feasible or better strategies between tested points.
Target operating profit is rounded upward to the next currency cent so a fractional-cent target is never reported as satisfied below its requested value.
All candidates retain the exact historical orders-to-visitors conversion ratio.
